newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries end higher amid short-covering.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries end higher amid short-covering.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities ended higher on Tuesday as dealers covered short positions ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy-making arm was scheduled to announce its intentions on Wednesday.
The Federal Open Market Committee was widely expected to leave monetary policy unchanged as it did at in May following a 25-basis-point hike at its March 25 convocation.
Analysts said an apparent slowdown in economic activity in the second quarter probably would be enough of a deterrent to keep to Federal Reserve from changing monetary policy in July.

Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan has said he would look more to signs of economic growth than to obvious statistical indicators in deciding whether to further tighten monetary policy. The Fed hiked the federal funds rate -- the interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans -- on March 25 and many economists expected further increases of at least 50 basis points before the end of the year.
Robert Dederick, chief economist and executive vice president at Northern Trust Co, said he was surprised by the bond market's strength given the data seen early in the session.
The National Association of Purchasing Management's June survey revealed an increase in manufacturing activity and an increase of 0.3 percent in leading economic indicators.

Dederick attributed the gains seen on Tuesday to market optimism that the Fed would not move on Wednesday. He saw a rebound in economic growth in the third quarter, but cautioned it "wouldn't happen on a dime given the inventory pickup seen recently."
Dederick said the bond market could be becoming too optimistic, with many players even shaking off the possibility of further tightening in August.
The Treasury's 30-year bond was trading up 20/32 at 98-18/32 to yield 6.74 percent.
In other trade, the five-year note was up 8/32 at 99-22/32 with a yield of 6.32 percent.

At the short end of the maturity curve, the three-month bill was down one basis point at 5.11 percent and the six-month bill was unchanged at 5.13 percent. The year bill was down two basis points at 5.34 percent.
